title: When a contact shared by two processes binds them at the first step
subject: Shared contacts between two rings, read with the canonical knot test on their space-time law, at lag 1 and in the linear case
conclusion: Two rings of at least three cells share one contact cell that both rings read. A contact that combines the two rings' proposals binds both rings at lag 1, every minimally decisive set of c(1) meeting both rings' own cells, exactly when its combiner is XOR or XNOR and neither ring rule is canalizing at its centre; otherwise either the canalizing ring decides alone or the contact's own first value fixes a proposal. A self-blind contact h(a_{m-1}, a_1, b_{n-1}, b_1), which both rings read but which does not read itself, binds at lag 1 exactly when its 4 x 4 table has no constant row and no constant column (22,874 of the 65,536 laws), so its parities u(a_{m-1}, a_1) + v(b_{n-1}, b_1) bind exactly when u and v are nonconstant. With linear or affine rings and an affine contact law the shared system is affine, and the contact binds at lag T exactly when the support of its row of M^T meets both rings.
